A nonlocal compensation lemma can be proved. It pays negative comb flux using a transverse strip at the distant saturated ends, and it still works when those ends occur at different distances. This gives a precisely delimited family with coefficient one, including configurations with
$$F=-2,\qquad A=D'=D_{\mathrm{union}}=0.$$
The full prescribed-source class remains open: the current hypotheses do not ensure that the required transverse strips are endpoint-free or that their physical deficits can always be allocated without overlap. Below I separate the proved result from that remaining extension.1. First refinement: every negative complete comb has debt exactly oneAlthough each end multiplicity lies in  $\{0,1,2\}$ , a complete comb’s flux cannot be  $-2$ .For a complete comb  $C$ , separate its strip memberships into directions parallel and perpendicular to its endpoint path.If a parallel strip contains either endpoint, it contains the entire straight endpoint path. Otherwise that path would cross a forced-blank extreme row or column. Consequently, both physical singleton end tiles lie in the same parallel strip. Parallel memberships therefore contribute equally to the sparse and saturated multiplicities.In the perpendicular direction, the strips are pairwise disjoint. Each end has perpendicular multiplicity zero or one. Thus
$$f_C:=m_{\mathrm{sat}}(C)-m_{\mathrm{sparse}}(C)
\in\{-1,0,1\}.$$
This includes the negative case
$$m_{\mathrm{sparse}}=2,\qquad m_{\mathrm{sat}}=1.$$
Let  $N_-$  and  $N_+$  count negative and positive complete-comb fluxes. Then
$$F=N_+-N_-,\qquad F\ge-N_-.$$
There is an immediate consequence for the entire retained class:
$$\boxed{F\ge-1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\Delta\ge0.}$$
Indeed, the accepted identity gives  $2\Delta\ge-1$ , while  $\Delta$  is an integer because the rectangle is even and  $|T|,|M|$  are integers. Hence any counterexample in this class would require  $F\le-2$ .The geometric work therefore begins with pairs of negative combs.2. An elementary physical-strip lemmaThe following partition identity will supply actual physical deficit.Let
$$Q=\{s,s+1\}\times\{\alpha,\ldots,\beta\}$$
be a horizontal strip of physical tiles, with  $s,\alpha$  even and  $\beta$  odd. Assume that  $Q$  contains no endpoints. Let  $\tau$  be the number of selected vertices in its two extreme columns.Delete those columns and partition the remaining rectangle into squares shifted horizontally by one vertex. If  $Q$  has  $n$  physical tiles and  $t$  selected vertices, then the shifted partition has  $n-1$  squares and  $t-\tau$  selected vertices. Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
D_Q&=2n-t,\\
D'_Q&=2(n-1)-(t-\tau),
\end{aligned}$$
so
$$\boxed{D_Q=2-\tau+D'_Q.} \tag{10}$$
Every shifted square has at most two selected vertices, giving  $D'_Q\ge0$ . Consequently:Two blank extreme columns force  $D_Q\ge2$ .One blank extreme column and one extreme column containing exactly one selection force  $D_Q\ge1$ .Here  $D_Q$  is the sum of deficits of original physical no- $P$  tiles. No endpoint charge appears in (10).3. A distant transverse strip forced by two combsI will call the transverse strip in the next lemma a rung.Remote-rung lemmaAfter a common tile-preserving reflection or transposition, suppose two prescribed complete combs have endpoint paths
$$P_L=\{u_L,\ldots,s_L\}\times\{a\},
\qquad
P_R=\{u_R,\ldots,s_R\}\times\{b\},$$
where: $a$  is odd,  $b$  is even, and  $b-a\ge5$ ; $u_L,u_R$  are odd and  $s_L,s_R$  are even;each top singleton end is sparse and each bottom singleton end is saturated;their axial intervals overlap:
$$\max(u_L,u_R)\le\min(s_L,s_R).$$
Put
$$s=\min(s_L,s_R)$$
and define the aligned physical strip
$$Q=\{s,s+1\}\times\{a+1,\ldots,b-1\}. \tag{11}$$
If  $Q$  contains no endpoints, then
$$\boxed{
D_Q\ge
\begin{cases}
2,&s_L=s_R,\\
1,&s_L\ne s_R.
\end{cases}}
\tag{12}$$
There is no restriction on the lengths of the two combs or on the distance from  $Q$  to their sparse ends.ProofIn this normal form, the left comb’s side supports lie at column  $a+1$  on odd endpoint rows and at column  $a-1$  on even endpoint rows. The right comb has side supports at column  $b-1$  on odd rows and at column  $b+1$  on even rows.Suppose first that the left comb ends at row  $s$ . Its prescribed support
$$(s-1,a+1)$$
already has  $(s-1,a)$  as its occupied neighbor. Thus
$$(s,a+1)$$
is forced blank.Its axial support
$$(s+1,a)$$
already has the terminal endpoint  $(s,a)$  as its occupied neighbor. Thus
$$(s+1,a+1)$$
is also forced blank.The left extreme column of  $Q$  is therefore completely blank. The reflected argument applies when the right comb ends at row  $s$ .The preceding support exists even for a comb of length two: the parity and overlap assumptions imply
$$\max(u_L,u_R)\le s-1.$$
If both combs end at row  $s$ , both extremes are blank. Equation (10) gives
$$D_Q=2+D'_Q\ge2.$$
If, instead, the right comb continues, its even terminal row is at least  $s+2$ . It therefore contains endpoints in both rows  $s,s+1$ . Its facing side support is
$$(s+1,b-1)\in T,$$
and that support forces  $(s,b-1)$  blank. The right extreme column of  $Q$  contains exactly one selected vertex.Thus the two extreme columns contain one selection in total, and (10) gives
$$D_Q=1+D'_Q\ge1.$$
The other unequal-length case is symmetric. ∎Why no matching export is being usedThe left comb’s physical receiver column pair is  $\{a-1,a\}$ , and the right comb’s is  $\{b,b+1\}$ . Both lie outside  $Q$ .The proof counts only the no- $P$  physical tiles strictly between those receiver bands. A prescribed side support may lie in such a tile, and is included in its actual  $t_Q$ . Neither a sparse negative raw half nor a saturated positive raw half is treated as a donor.This directly avoids the partial-receiver problem in the fixed-radius obstacle.4. A proved compensation theorem for negative fluxHere is a clean family in which the remote-rung lemma settles the coefficient-one bound.Theorem: compensation by disjoint remote rungsWork at the fixed terminal representative where the accepted ledger holds. Suppose all but at most one negative complete comb can be paired so that each pair satisfies the remote-rung lemma. Require that the chosen rungs:contain no endpoints;lie outside the original mouth union  $G$ ;are pairwise disjoint as sets of physical tiles.Then
$$\boxed{|T|+|M|\le mn/2.}$$
The same conclusion applies to the initial objective through the retained normalization.ProofLet  $N_-$  be the number of negative combs, and let
$$q=\left\lfloor\frac{N_-}{2}\right\rfloor$$
be the number of chosen pairs.Each rung contributes at least one physical no- $P$  deficit. Because the rungs are outside  $G$  and pairwise disjoint, these contributions are distinct terms of the exterior physical deficit included in  $R$ . Hence
$$R\ge q.$$
Using the exact accepted identity once,
$$\begin{aligned}
2\Delta
&=F+A+D'+D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R\\
&\ge -N_-+2q\\
&\ge-1.
\end{aligned}$$
Integrality gives  $\Delta\ge0$ . ∎This theorem permits:arbitrarily long combs;unequal distances to their saturated ends;all allowed orientations, pair by pair;arbitrary original source-mouth crossings;a single unpaired negative comb.The pairing conditions concern distant geometry and physical capacity. They impose no fixed-radius allocation.A more economical version allows any number  $q$  of usable rungs satisfying
$$F+2q\ge-1.$$
Positive comb flux can therefore reduce how many negative combs need geometric payment.5. A capacity version that allows some overlapsThe disjoint-exterior condition is convenient but can be weakened, especially when the paired saturated tips are aligned.For each chosen rung  $Q_j$ , set
$$\beta_j=
\begin{cases}
0,&\text{its two saturated tips are aligned},\\
1,&\text{one comb continues beyond the other}.
\end{cases}$$
The geometric lemma proves
$$D_{Q_j}\ge2-\beta_j.$$
Assign the rung a bookkeeping weight
$$w_j=
\begin{cases}
1,&\beta_j=0,\\
2,&\beta_j=1.
\end{cases}$$
Then every rung provides
$$w_jD_{Q_j}\ge2.$$
For a physical no- $P$  tile  $Q$ , let  $m_Q\in\{0,1,2\}$  be its original source-mouth multiplicity. The part of its deficit available in
$$D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R_{\mathrm{noP}}$$
has coefficient  $2-m_Q$ .It is sufficient to impose, on every positive-deficit physical no- $P$  tile,
$$\boxed{\sum_{j:\,Q\subseteq Q_j}w_j\le2-m_Q.} \tag{13}$$
Here  $R_{\mathrm{noP}}$  denotes only the physical no- $P$  deficit outside  $G$ .Under (13),
$$\begin{aligned}
\sum_jw_jD_{Q_j}
&\le \sum_Q(2-m_Q)d_Q\\
&=D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R_{\mathrm{noP}}\\
&\le D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus  $q$  rungs give
$$2\Delta\ge F+2q,$$
with the same coefficient-one conclusion when  $F+2q\ge-1$ .This identifies the capacities exactly:An unequal-length rung uses the full physical deficit on its tiles. Such a rung must avoid already allocated mouth capacity unless the deficit there is zero.An aligned cap needs only half of each physical deficit in the original  $\Delta$ -ledger. It can cross a singly covered mouth strip, or another aligned cap outside  $G$ , subject to (13).No positive deficit can be used beyond its displayed capacity.This is a single allocation against the accepted identity. It does not add the earlier crossing-loss estimate as another source of payment.6. Explicit arbitrary-length example with zero original mouth paymentThe new family is nonempty even in the case that defeats payment based only on the original strip deficits.Take a downward prescribed source of width  $10$ , depth  $h\ge1$ , with chamber origin  $(2,3)$ . Put
$$y_0=2h+4.$$
Its mouth is
$$\{y_0,y_0+1\}\times\{4,\ldots,11\}.$$
Add two downward complete combs:a left comb in column  $5$ , with endpoints
$$y_0+1,\ldots,y_0+2\ell_L;$$
a right comb in column  $10$ , with endpoints
$$y_0+1,\ldots,y_0+2\ell_R,$$
where  $\ell_L,\ell_R\ge1$ .Use consecutive matching. Their prescribed side supports are:left comb: column  $6$  at odd endpoint rows and column  $4$  at even endpoint rows;right comb: column  $9$  at odd endpoint rows and column  $11$  at even endpoint rows.Include the axial supports at row  $y_0$  and one row beyond each terminal endpoint. Also select
$$(y_0,7),\qquad(y_0,8).$$
Original mouth countThe physical mouth has four tiles:ColumnsPhysical contents $4,5$ Left sparse singleton end $6,7$ Two selected vertices $8,9$ Two selected vertices $10,11$ Right sparse singleton endHence
$$D_{\mathrm{mouth}}=0.$$
After deleting extreme columns  $4,11$ , the shifted endpoint squares at columns  $5,6$  and  $9,10$  each have  $(p,t)=(1,2)$ . The middle square at columns  $7,8$  contains the selected pair. Thus
$$D'_{\mathrm{mouth}}=0.$$
Both sparse ends belong to the sole source mouth, and neither saturated end does. Therefore
$$F=-2,\qquad A=0.$$
Remote physical paymentSuppose  $\ell_L<\ell_R$ , and put
$$s=y_0+2\ell_L.$$
Select the additional pair
$$(s,7),\qquad(s,8).$$
The remote rung is
$$Q=\{s,s+1\}\times\{6,7,8,9\}.$$
Its left extreme column is blank. Its right extreme contains the longer comb’s prescribed support at  $(s+1,9)$ . Along with the added selected pair, this gives three selections in two physical tiles:
$$D_Q=4-3=1.$$
Thus the unequal-length bound is attained locally. If the lengths are equal, both extreme columns are blank and the same selected pair gives
$$D_Q=2.$$
FeasibilityThe two comb endpoint columns are separated by five. Their side supports are separated from one another and from the source’s supports. At the junction with the mouth, the nearest potentially problematic source supports are diagonal to the new occupied vertices.Each prescribed support retains its intended endpoint as its sole occupied neighbor. Each of the two added horizontal pairs is isolated in the occupied graph: the prescribed side supports near it occur diagonally, and the directly adjacent sites are blank.The source and the two combs are therefore distinct complete endpoint components. Leaving other sites blank gives a feasible construction for every indicated parameter choice.The rung’s distance from the original mouth tends to infinity with
$$\min(\ell_L,\ell_R).$$
This example proves that the family handles zero original strip payment and unbounded transport distance. Its blank exterior supplies other donors too, so it is not being claimed as a new “no nearer donor” construction; your stronger all-radius obstacle remains the relevant statement for that issue.7. A second closure lemma at the source levelThere is also a direct way to compensate negative flux when the combs stay inside the full region between a source’s arms. It uses the same partition principle, without pairing the comb ends.For a downward source in the relative coordinates of your question, define its full inner cavity
$$C_H=\{2,\ldots,r+1\}\times\{1,\ldots,w-2\},
\qquad r=2h+2.$$
This includes the mouth and all the physical row bands between the arms below the chamber.Whole-cavity closure lemmaAssume every endpoint component meeting  $C_H$  is a complete prescribed comb whose entire endpoint set is contained in  $C_H$ . Arbitrary feasible selections are allowed.Then
$$\boxed{D_{C_H}=2+D'_{C_H}\ge2.} \tag{14}$$
Here both deficit sums use their respective partitions of the cavity;  $D_{C_H}$  is original physical deficit.ProofThe two boundary columns  $1,w-2$  contain precisely the prescribed inside supports at rows
$$3,5,\ldots,r-1.$$
Every other site in those columns is forced blank by the neighboring prescribed supports, including the axial supports at the final row. Deleting the two columns therefore removes exactly  $2h$  selected vertices and no endpoints.The physical cavity has
$$n=\frac{(h+1)(w-2)}2$$
tiles. Its horizontally shifted, trimmed partition has
$$n'=\frac{(h+1)(w-4)}2$$
squares. Thus
$$n-n'=h+1.$$
Let  $E,E'$  be the total raw endpoint-square weights in the two cavity partitions. The raw partition equations give
$$D_{C_H}-D'_{C_H}
=
2(n-n')-2h+E-E'
=
2+E-E'.$$
The closure hypothesis ensures that every comb is counted wholly in both partitions. By the accepted complete-comb phase tables,
$$E=E'=0.$$
Equation (14) follows. ∎The whole-comb condition is doing real work. It cancels the sparse and saturated contributions over the complete cavity; it does not convert a partial negative end into a donor.Consequence for disjoint closed cavitiesIf every one of the  $B$  sources has such a cavity and these cavities are pairwise disjoint as physical tile sets, then
$$D_{\mathrm{all\ physical\ no}\text{-}P}
\ge\sum_H D_{C_H}\ge2B.$$
The original whole-receiver ledger gives
$$\boxed{\Delta\ge B.}$$
This is a strict-margin family allowing negative mouth flux and arbitrarily deep combs.For example, in relative coordinates, take even  $w\ge12$ ,  $h\ge2$ , and add complete vertical combs in columns  $3$  and  $8$ , both with endpoints at rows  $5,\ldots,r$ . Give the left comb side supports in column  $4$  on odd rows and column  $2$  on even rows; give the right comb supports in column  $7$  on odd rows and column  $9$  on even rows. Include axial supports at rows  $4,r+1$ .Their top singleton ends are saturated, their bottom singleton ends are sparse, and only the sparse ends lie in the source mouth. Thus  $F=-2$ . The prescribed supports are compatible, and both complete combs lie in  $C_H$ , so (14) supplies the compensation. The starting rows may also be staggered, provided the complete combs remain in the cavity.8. What remains openThe proved progress is that negative comb flux can be paid by distant original physical deficit in two concrete settings:transverse strips between suitable parallel combs, including unequal terminal heights;an entire source cavity closed under complete comb components.Neither proof uses a fixed radius, a partial endpoint charge, or a second copy of an actual matching contribution.The missing general step is a geometric existence-and-capacity theorem. The retained full-class hypotheses do not currently ensure that:enough negative combs admit partners with compatible directions and overlapping axial ranges;the separating transverse regions contain no foreign endpoints;those regions have enough independently usable physical capacity;alternatively, larger regions can be closed under complete components while keeping a controlled boundary contribution.Unequal terminal heights have been removed as an obstruction to the rung argument. Endpoint intrusions and competing claims on the same distant donors remain substantive obstacles.For an initial-pair formulation, the new rung or cavity conditions should be imposed at the terminal representative, or their preservation should be separately established for the normalization being used. Preservation of the original mouth data alone does not assert preservation of an arbitrary new exterior region.The strongest result established here is therefore the remote-rung compensation theorem, with the whole-cavity lemma providing a second source-level closure mechanism. A proof for every configuration in the full prescribed-source class is still missing.
